findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt matchesOrderType plus ui/SettingsScreen.kt order type selector
findings.claim: The four per-condition options are rendered as mutually exclusive buttons but the shared predicate they reuse is not a partition: MOSTRADOR matches Picap transfer orders because Picap labels them Mostrador, and TRASLADO matches any order whose delivery address is Cruz Verde or a saved address without checking that it is a transfer. A driver who picks Mostrador or Traslado for one condition can therefore still auto-accept orders from the other category. This exact overlap already exists in the base global filter and in the base MainActivity selector, so it is inherited behavior rather than a regression.
proof_refs: At HEAD MyAccessibilityService line 1177 computes isMostrador and the MOSTRADOR branch at line 1183 accepts any order whose servicio contains Mostrador, so transfer orders already passed the MOSTRADOR filter before this change

MainActivity lines 528 to 556 already render four exclusive segmented buttons OMS Mostrador Traslado Todos over that same overlapping predicate, and the new selector in SettingsScreen reproduces it verbatim including button order and labels

The new matchesOrderType TRASLADO arm at MyAccessibilityService line 1274 delegates to trasladoOk which only inspects direccionEntrega, so any order addressed to Cruz Verde or a saved address matches regardless of servicio
